standard_prerequisites.name: Glueing pairs (R -> R', f), glueable modules and the glued module M-tilde
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: fixed earlier in the same section, used at proof lines 25709-25710 and 25720
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction from an arbitrary M to a glueable one, which is the first half of the converse direction.

standard_prerequisites.name: The flatness criterion via Tor_1^R(M, N) = 0, and Lazard's theorem that a flat module is a filtered colimit of finite free modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the problem into a Tor-vanishing statement and lets the f-action be transferred to the base change.

standard_prerequisites.name: The change-of-rings spectral sequence for Tor and the exact sequence 0 -> R -> R' oplus R_f -> (R')_f -> 0
standard_prerequisites.use: Computes Tor_i^R(M tensor_R R', N) from Tor_i^R(R', N) and produces the f-action statement.

core_obligations: Dispose of the easy direction by flat base change (proof lines 25716-25717).

For the converse, introduce the glued module M-tilde and show that if M-tilde is flat then Ker(M -> M-tilde) tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) = 0, hence M = M-tilde, so that one may assume M glueable (proof lines 25720-25727).
Reduce flatness to the vanishing of Tor_1^R(M, N) for all R-modules N, using the flatness criterion (proof lines 25728-25730).
From the exact sequence 0 -> R -> R' oplus R_f -> (R')_f -> 0 deduce that f is a nonzerodivisor on Tor_1^R(R', N) and invertible on Tor_i^R(R', N) for i >= 2 (proof lines 25733-25744).

Transfer that conclusion to Tor_i^R(M tensor_R R', N) using the change-of-rings spectral sequence and the identification of M tensor_R R' as a filtered colimit of finite free R'-modules, so that f acts on Tor_1 of the base change as a nonzerodivisor and is invertible on Tor_i for i >= 2 (proof lines 25745-25755).

Use the long exact Tors sequence of 0 -> M -> M tensor_R R' oplus M_f -> M tensor_R (R')_f -> 0, whose relevant portion is displayed, together with the f-action statements just established, to conclude Tor_1^R(M, N) = 0 (proof lines 25756-25770).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a glueing pair (R -> R', f) and an arbitrary R-module M that is not assumed glueable, and asserts that M is flat over R exactly when M tensor_R R' is flat over R' and M_f is flat over R_f (source lines 25707-25713). One direction is base change, but the other forces the proof to first reduce to the glueable case: it introduces the glued module M-tilde, and if that is flat it applies the flat Tors criterion to the sequence 0 -> Ker(M -> M-tilde) -> M -> M-tilde -> 0 to conclude that Ker(M -> M-tilde) tensor_R (R' oplus R_f) vanishes, whence M = M-tilde by the faithfulness lemma (proof lines 25716-25727). The substantive part is then the Tors computation. From the exact sequence 0 -> R -> R' oplus R_f -> (R')_f -> 0 the proof reads off that f is a nonzerodivisor on Tor_1^R(R', N) and invertible on Tor_i^R(R', N) for i >= 2 (proof lines 25733-25744), transfers that to Tor_i^R(M tensor_R R', N) using flatness of M tensor_R R' over R' together with the change-of-rings spectral sequence and the Lazard filtered-colimit description (proof lines 25745-25755), and finally feeds it into the long exact Tors sequence of the glueable sequence 0 -> M -> M tensor_R R' oplus M_f -> M tensor_R (R')_f -> 0 to force Tor_1^R(M, N) = 0 (proof lines 25756-25770). The non-routine content is the two-step comparison of the f-action on the two families of Tor modules, which is what makes the Tors criterion applyable.
